skill.name: db-migration
skill.description: Guides Alembic migration setup and schema changes for SQLModel and FastAPI projects, including generation, upgrades, rollbacks, data migrations, and review checklists.
skill.summary: Manage Alembic migrations for SQLModel and FastAPI projects.
skill.author: Awais68

security_audit.summary: The verifier script finding is a false positive; it only validates skill metadata. Most SKILL.md findings are Markdown backtick noise, but the skill does direct users to run mutable Alembic commands and includes destructive migration examples. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found, but database safety controls should be strengthened.

remediation.suggestion: State that upgrade, downgrade, and revision commands require explicit user approval and environment confirmation before execution.
Require backups, restore tests, and production approval before downgrade base, drop table, drop column, or drop type examples.
Replace user:pass connection strings with environment-variable or secret-manager placeholders.

remediation.issue: Misleading no data loss checklist item
remediation.suggestion: Replace drop-based no-data-loss guidance with additive migrations, backfills, archival plans, and verified rollback limits.

static_findings.snippet: | `alembic init alembic` | Initialize Alembic in project |
| `alembic revision --autogenerate -m "message"` | Generate migration from model changes |
| `alembic upgrade head` | Apply all pending migrations |
| `alembic upgrade +1` | Apply one migration at a time |
- [ ] **Test migrations**: Run `alembic upgrade` then `alembic downgrade` in test
- [ ] **No data loss**: Use `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS`, `DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS`
| `@fastapi-app` | Migrations run at startup or via CLI |
| `@jwt-auth` | May need to handle auth during migrations |

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Database Operation Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill includes downgrade-to-base, drop table, drop column, drop type, and bulk update examples. These operations can delete or corrupt production data without backup and approval controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly describe downgrade base and drop operations. These are legitimate migration actions, but the data-loss risk is clear and high impact.

semantic_findings.title: Plaintext Database URL Examples
semantic_findings.description: The examples show database connection URLs with user and password placeholders inside configuration. This can normalize storing credentials in committed files instead of secret-managed configuration.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The values appear to be placeholders, not real secrets. The risk is guidance quality because users may copy the pattern into project files.

content.value_statement: Database schema changes can break applications or lose data when they are handled manually. This skill guides Alembic setup, migration generation, rollback planning, and review for SQLModel and FastAPI projects.
actual_capabilities: Explains Alembic initialization and configuration for SQLModel metadata.
Guides generation, inspection, upgrade, and rollback commands for migrations.
Shows patterns for tables, columns, indexes, foreign keys, enums, and batch data updates.
Provides review checklists for upgrade and downgrade testing.
Describes integration points with FastAPI, SQLModel CRUD, and authentication changes.
limitations: Does not verify a live database schema by itself.
Examples use placeholder names and require project-specific adaptation.
Rollback and drop operations can destroy data without backups.
Does not replace DBA review for production migrations.

use_cases.title: Add a Model Table
use_cases.description: Plan an Alembic revision for a new SQLModel table, including indexes, constraints, and a downgrade path.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Migrations
use_cases.description: Create a staged migration checklist with history checks, test upgrades, and rollback boundaries.

use_cases.title: Review Generated Revisions
use_cases.description: Check autogenerated migrations for unintended drops, missing constraints, data movement, and release risk.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Alembic
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new project
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me initialize Alembic for a FastAPI SQLModel project. Show the files to configure and explain each setting.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Revision
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a migration after model changes
prompt_templates.prompt: I changed these SQLModel models: [describe changes]. Guide me through generating and reviewing an Alembic migration safely.

prompt_templates.title: Review Rollback Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this migration plan for upgrade and downgrade safety. Identify data loss risks, missing indexes, and required test steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design Data Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production-safe Alembic data migration for a large table. Include batching, validation, rollback limits, and release checks.

output_examples.input: I need to add a fees table to a SQLModel app.
output: Recommended revision name and generation approach.
Checklist for columns, indexes, foreign keys, and downgrade order.
Test plan for applying and rolling back in a disposable database.

output_examples.input: Check whether my downgrade plan is safe for release.
output: Summary of operations that may remove data.
Required backup, restore, and approval steps before production use.
Safer alternatives for reversible or phased migrations.

output_examples.input: Plan a data migration for updating many status values.
output: Validation checks before and after the migration.
Rollback limits and monitoring items for the release window.

best_practices: Run migrations against a disposable database before any shared environment.
Review autogenerated revisions for unintended table, column, index, or constraint changes.
Take backups and define rollback limits before production upgrades.
anti_patterns: Running downgrade base against any database that contains important data.
Committing placeholder database credentials without replacing them with secure configuration.
Accepting autogenerated migrations without checking data migrations and constraints.

faq.question: Does this skill run migrations automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Users or agents must run commands with explicit approval.

faq.question: Can it be used with PostgreSQL?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples include PostgreSQL-oriented Alembic and SQLModel patterns.

faq.question: Does it support production migrations?
faq.answer: It can help plan them, but production changes still need backups, testing, and operational approval.

faq.question: Can it create data migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for batch updates and status changes inside Alembic revisions.

faq.question: Is it limited to SQLModel?
faq.answer: The examples focus on SQLModel and FastAPI, but many Alembic concepts also apply to SQLAlchemy projects.

faq.question: What is the main safety concern?
faq.answer: Downgrades, drops, and data updates can remove or corrupt data when used without backups and review.
